page: Microsoft Azure D192lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system provides 384.0 GB of memory, resulting in a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes 11,339 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, registering top-tier results for both cached small-block and uncached large-block read/write operations. Single-threaded compression and multi-threaded decompression also rank in the top 10%. For database and caching workloads, the server achieves top-tier throughput in Redis SET operations and strong PassMark database performance. Large-model LLM inference prompt processing ranks in the top 10%, though text generation speeds for smaller models fall into the bottom 25%, highlighting a performance tradeoff in sequential generation tasks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D192lds_v7 offers high compute density and substantial local storage capacity, making it a viable option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio represents a deliberate tradeoff, reducing memory overhead costs while maximizing raw processing power. This configuration is suitable for multi-threaded batch processing, high-throughput web serving, cryptographic operations, and database workloads that can operate within the 384.0 GB memory limit while leveraging the 11,339 GB local disk.
description: Microsoft Azure D192lds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server from the Dldsv7 family, powered by a 192-vCPU Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 384.0 GB of RAM, establishing a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core, and includes 11,339 GB of local storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the server lacks GPU accelerators but supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and high-throughput Redis operations. However, single-core CPU performance is average, and small-model LLM text generation is relatively weak. This server is designed for compute-intensive, multi-threaded workloads, high-throughput web serving, and local-storage-heavy database operations that do not require high memory-to-CPU ratios.
